main_body: Steel column: a wide capital drum at the top (rows 8-16), a fluted shaft with ring bands (rows 17-40), and a base drum (rows 41-47).
top_band: Light grey rounded top slab, rows 9-12 (about 4 rows), with a brighter highlight on row 9-10. A lighter front-edge row at 13 carries dark rivet dots.
evidence: In the middle column the light top slab (rows 9-12) is a few rows tall and has rounded, outlined corners. Row 13 is a lighter edge with dark dots, and rows 14-16 are a dark underside, so the cap overhangs the shaft. The base drum repeats the pattern with a light top and a dark front. The top is clearer than a 1-2px rim, though it is a fairly flat rectangular slab rather than an ellipse. It is borderline but reads as a surface above a front face.

style.evidence: The grey ramp has only about 4 steps (white-grey highlight, light, mid, dark). The outline is a neutral dark grey-black with little tint, which gives a sticker look. The shaft flutes and cap faces are mostly flat fills with no grain or speckle, and no per-surface texture dots like the stall and well references. Most tiles carry only 3-5 colours, so it is clearly thinner than the Beodeul props.
